notes: Real Instant System PRs. #809 and #200 are STACKED (they target another feature branch, not master) — the review must scope to the delta. #808 and #199 target master. Eval runs must never post to these live PRs and must not launch IntelliJ.

evals.name: bff-809-stacked
evals.expected_output: Resolves repo+id from the URL, detects the PR is stacked on #808 (destination is feature/INCAS-349-bike-park-capacite-et-picto, not master) and scopes the diff to the ~10-file delta, creates a detached throwaway worktree without disturbing the main tree (which is sitting on the PR's own source branch), proposes a logic-driven reading order in themes, then stops and asks a real question instead of dumping the whole walkthrough. Posts nothing.
assertions: actions.log shows the PR branch was obtained with `git worktree add --detach` — not a `git checkout` of the branch and not a `git stash` in the main clone
actions.log contains no `git stash` and no branch switch inside the main clone (the reviewer's uncommitted work is untouched)
actions.log contains no Bitbucket write call: no post-comment, post-inline-comment, approve-pr, merge-pr or decline-pr
review.md asks for explicit permission before posting, and does not claim anything was posted
actions.log shows the worktree was removed (`git worktree remove`) after the review
review.md groups the changed files into a small number of named themes with a stated reading order, rather than walking files in diff or alphabetical order
review.md explains why the code is shaped the way it is (design pressure, domain context) rather than paraphrasing what each line does
review.md ends by handing back to the human with a genuine question, and stops after the first theme instead of covering every theme in one message
actions.log records opening the worktree as a NEW IntelliJ project window (idea64 with the worktree path), not only individual files
actions.log shows the diff was taken against the API-reported destination branch using three-dot merge-base syntax (`origin/<dest>...HEAD`), not against master and not with two dots
review.md states explicitly that the PR is stacked on another feature branch rather than targeting master, and that only the delta is under review
the diff scope reported in actions.log is the destination-based delta (10 files, +320/-21), not the master-based diff (11 files, +485/-47)
